'''Akashi no Kuni no Miyatsuko''' (''akashi no kuni no miyatsuko'', ''akashi kokuzō'') was a {{ill|kuni no miyatsuko|ja|国造}} who ruled '''Akashi Province''' — present-day {{ill|East Harima|ja|東播磨県民局|lt=East Harima}}, {{ill|Shinmei|ja|神明}}, and {{ill|Miki, Hyōgo|ja|三木市|lt=Miki City}} in Hyōgo Prefecture.

== Overview ==
=== Ancestry ===
*According to the "Kokuzō Hongi" of the ''{{ill|Sendai Kuji Hongi|ja|先代旧事本紀}}'', '''Tsumiji-no-Sukune''', a son of Yashiro-no-Sukune of the same line as the {{ill|Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|倭国造|lt=Yamato-no-Atai}}, was appointed kuni no miyatsuko during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ja|応神天皇|lt=Emperor Ōjin|lt_ja=応神朝}}.

=== Clan ===
'''{{ill|Ama clan|ja|海氏}}''' (''ama-uji''; {{ill|kabane|ja|カバネ|lt=kabane|lt_ja=姓}} of {{ill|Atai (kabane)|ja|直 (姓)|lt=Atai|lt_ja=直}}). In the sixth month of {{ill|Jingo-keiun|ja|神護景雲}} 3, they were granted the surname '''Yamato-Akashi-no-Muraji'''. The later {{ill|Akashi clan|ja|明石氏}} of the {{ill|Akamatsu clan|ja|赤松氏|lt=Akamatsu-line}} branch falsely claimed descent from the {{ill|Murakami Genji|ja|村上源氏}}, but some scholars argue they were actually descendants of the kuni no miyatsuko.<ref>{{ill|Ōta Akira|ja|太田亮}}, "Akashi" in ''Seishi Kakei Daijiten'', 1942, p.31.</ref>

The clan's relatives included the {{ill|Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|倭国造}}, the {{ill|Kubiki no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|久比岐国造}}, and the {{ill|Aomi clan|ja|青海氏}}.

== Base ==
'''Akashi-gō''' in {{ill|Akashi District|ja|明石郡}}, {{ill|Harima Province|ja|播磨国}}.

To the north of the Akashi no Kuni no Miyatsuko was the {{ill|Harima-Kamo no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|針間鴨国造}}; across the Ten River to the west was the {{ill|Harima no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|針間国造}}.

== Tutelary deity ==
'''{{ill|Watatsumi Shrine (Kobe)|ja|海神社 (神戸市)|lt=Watatsumi Shrine|lt_ja=海神社}}''', the only {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社}} among the {{ill|shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} of {{ill|Akashi District|ja|明石郡}}. It enshrines the sea deity, the clan's ancestral deity.
